findings.claim: The new casual-presentation rule forbids file paths and rule/FACT/ACDSL IDs in `change`, but the same skill still mandates machine-read `change` strings that consist of exactly those (step 4b eviction: `set projected="false" on <ID>` / `remove <ID> from <skill> context:`; step 2 declaration: `declare <entry-ID> in skills/<path>/SKILL.md acdsl-context:`), with no exemption like smine-permissions grants its rule string. On a casual install every such proposal violates one of the two contracts, and smine-consolidate's casual jargon sweep (§4 L51) then rewrites `change` and moves the ID into anchor/target — removing the literal form smine-apply step 4(d) dispatches the eviction route on. Same class in smine-skills L65: a Workflows entry's `change` must be "author `workflows/<name>.js` under `<target>`", a file path the casual rule bans.
findings.fix: Exempt the machine-read change forms (eviction `set projected=…`/`remove <ID> from …`, `declare <ID> in …`, Workflows `author workflows/<name>.js …`) from the casual rule in smine-context/smine-memory/smine-skills and from smine-consolidate's casual sweep, the way smine-permissions keeps its rule string in `change`.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-context L33 (casual rule lists `change` among prose fields that carry no paths/IDs), L48 and L71 (change text prescribed with entry IDs and skill paths); smine-consolidate L51 (casual sweep rewords mutable entries whose `change` carries IDs/paths, moving content to target/anchor); smine-apply L31 route (d) keyed on the `set projected="false" on <ID>` / `remove <ID> from <skill> context:` change forms; smine-permissions L33 shows the explicit exemption pattern the other skills lack; smine-skills L65 Workflows change format with a path. Trigger: audience: casual + a context-use present-irrelevant aggregate over >=5 sessions (or a needed-not-present declaration amendment). Not covered by known.json (MAJ-61 concerns lockout of context routes editing skill files, not this field contract).

findings.claim: A casual-locked proposal is never archived, removed or status-changed: step 4 only sets the vote's disposition `casual-locked` (terminal, so the vote drains from the sidecar) and leaves the entry `proposed` in skills.json. It therefore resurfaces on the /proposals page for another vote, and in decide/always auto-apply it is a candidate again every night (step 5 candidates = every remaining `proposed` entry not voted this run), re-locked and re-ledgered each run. Reachable on a casual install for skills edit entries written before the audience switch, or re-homed into skills.json by smine-consolidate §2, which has no lockout check.
findings.fix: On casual-locked, also set the entry's status to `rejected` (or archive it to rejected.md with reason `casual lockout`) and remove it from skills.json like the other terminal outcomes, so it is neither re-voted nor re-picked by auto-apply.
findings.evidence: Re-read smine-apply L31 (lockout: 'do not touch the skill — set the proposal's disposition casual-locked with a one-line note'; the archive-and-remove sentence closes the implemented path only), L32-36 (auto-apply candidates: every remaining `proposed` entry, only entries voted this run excluded), L41-43 (casual-locked is a terminal outcome appended to votes-archive.jsonl, draining the vote); smine-skills L45 drops such candidates only at extraction and L59 reconciliation does not drop locked ones; smine-consolidate L37-41 re-homes into skills.json with no lockout. Spec item 89 (untouched skill + disposition) holds; the defect is the entry's lifecycle after the lock.
